outputs: Psychological counseling responses with proactive questioning timing and strategy recommendations
Proactive questioning strategies and conversational responses in psychological counseling

changes_made.explanation: Minor normalization of model names to standard capitalization. All extracted metadata was correct and relevant.

Normalized metric variants to base forms (ROUGE-1/ROUGE-L→ROUGE, BLEU-2/BLEU-4→BLEU). Kept SFR and PQR as they are task-specific automatic metrics for proactive questioning evaluation. Removed duplicate/abbreviated forms.
No LLM-as-judge evaluation was conducted in this paper. The paper uses LLMs for data annotation and client simulation, but not for judging generated outputs post-generation.

guideline: Evaluators scored each conversation turn on four metrics: Strategy Effectiveness (0-2), Reasoning Coherence (0-2), Professionalism (0-3), and Ethical Safety (0-1). Evaluation conducted by three psychology graduate students and one senior counselor with standardized training.
The evaluation team used scoring criteria for Strategy Effectiveness (SE), Reasoning Coherence (RC), Professionalism (Prof), and Ethical Safety (ES), with detailed scales for each.
Evaluators scored each model on Strategy Effectiveness (SE), Reasoning Coherence (RC), Professionalism (Prof) and Ethical safety using predefined rating scales.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated guideline descriptions into one comprehensive statement. Removed redundant criteria entries and normalized capitalization. Combined multiple guideline descriptions that were essentially saying the same thing.

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. The paper focuses on psychological dialogue generation with proactive questioning strategies. Automatic metrics include both standard NLG metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore) and task-specific metrics (SFR, PQR) for proactive questioning evaluation. Human evaluation was comprehensive with psychology experts. No LLM-as-judge evaluation was conducted.
